items.title: Write the test runner consolidation decision document and commit it to docs/requirements/decisions/
items.context: Create docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md. Required sections: (1) Current state pinned with numbers (151 *-smoke.ts files, ~70,280 lines total, 258 test:* npm scripts (111 in root package.json + 147 in packages/main/package.json), 49 scripts/verify-*.mjs, the dist-standalone-executable pattern via `node packages/main/dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js` consistent with testing-infra.md's general-black-box-command validation entry); (2) The three paths considered (A vitest migration, B in-house runner + manifest + c8, C B minus c8) with concrete pros/cons referencing the existing testing-infra.md project-native validation policy; (3) The chosen path (B) with explicit rationale: smokes are spawn-CLI integration scenarios not unit tests, the dist-standalone-executable pattern aligns with testing-infra.md's project-native validation policy, vitest migration would conflict with that policy, an in-house manifest+runner wraps the existing 70k lines without rewriting them and delivers CI speedup (parallel) + coverage (c8) + newcomer ergonomics (single test:all entry + selectable smokes) simultaneously; (4) The follow-up Lattice story decomposition: B1 in-house runner skeleton + manifest format + test:all entry, B2 collapse 258 test:* scripts into manifest entries (mechanical), B3 c8 coverage instrumentation + test:coverage entry, optional B4 tag/select UX improvements. Each follow-up story spec must include a one-paragraph scope sketch so future story_create calls can quote it verbatim. After: the file exists; `git log -- docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md` shows a commit; `grep -c '## ' docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md` >= 4 (the required sections).
items.userSees: `ls docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md` succeeds; opening the file shows the 4 sections (current state / paths considered / chosen path with rationale / follow-up B1-B4 stories) populated with concrete content.

happy.desc: ls docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md exits 0 -> file exists; WHY: primary deliverable existence check

grep -c "^## " docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md >= 4 -> doc has at least 4 H2 sections; WHY: enforces the 4 required sections contract (current state, paths considered, chosen path, follow-up)
grep -q 151 the doc exits 0 -> pinned smoke count present; WHY: current-state section must contain the audited 151 smoke file count
grep -qE 70[,.]?280 the doc exits 0 -> pinned line count present (allowing comma or period separator); WHY: current-state section must contain ~70,280 lines figure
grep -q 258 the doc exits 0 -> pinned test:* script count present; WHY: current-state section must contain 258 test:* npm scripts
grep -q 49 the doc exits 0 -> pinned verify script count present; WHY: current-state section must contain 49 verify scripts
grep -qiE (path.*A|option.*A|vitest) the doc exits 0 -> Path A (vitest) is named; WHY: paths-considered section must discuss vitest migration
grep -qi in-house the doc exits 0 -> Path B (in-house runner) is named; WHY: paths-considered section must discuss the in-house runner option
grep -qi testing-infra the doc exits 0 -> rationale references testing-infra.md; WHY: chosen-path rationale must explicitly reference the existing project-native validation policy
for B1 B2 B3 B4 grep each in the doc -> all four follow-up story IDs present; WHY: follow-up section must decompose into B1 B2 B3 B4
git log --oneline -- docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md produces at least 1 line -> file is committed; WHY: story requires a commit touching this path

edge.desc: section count boundary: grep -c ^## returns exactly 4 or more, never 3 -> catch off-by-one where a heading is missing or malformed (missing space after ##); WHY: boundary check on minimum section count
B4 is present even if marked optional -> grep -qi B4 exits 0; WHY: spec says B4 may be noted as optional but must still appear in the decomposition
wc -l > 30 -> doc has substantive content not a stub; WHY: catch degenerate case where sections exist as headings but bodies are empty
grep -qi c8 the doc exits 0 -> c8 coverage tool is mentioned; WHY: Path B and C both involve c8; its absence means paths-considered is incomplete

adversarial.desc: git diff main -- docs/requirements/decisions/testing-infra.md | wc -l returns 0 -> testing-infra.md is byte-identical to main; WHY: over-reach guard (b) no other decision doc may be modified

git diff main -- docs/requirements/decisions/testing-completeness.md | wc -l returns 0 -> testing-completeness.md is byte-identical to main; WHY: over-reach guard (b) no other decision doc may be modified
git diff --name-only main -- packages/ | wc -l returns 0 -> no code files in packages/ touched; WHY: over-reach guard (c) ZERO code change story
git diff --name-only main -- package.json | wc -l returns 0 -> root package.json untouched; WHY: over-reach guard (c) no package.json edits allowed
git diff --name-only main -- scripts/ | wc -l returns 0 -> no scripts/ edits; WHY: over-reach guard (c) no scripts changes in a doc-only story

git diff --name-only main -- docs/requirements/decisions/ | grep -v test-runner-consolidation-plan.md | wc -l returns 0 -> only the target file changed in decisions/; WHY: generalized over-reach guard catches edits to ANY other decision doc
4-section minimum is a hard gate: count=$(grep -c ^## ...) test >= 4 -> ENFORCED; WHY: adversarial guard (d) if any section heading is deleted or renamed to H3 the contract must fail
